courses.term: Spring 2026 course record; the uploaded syllabus document is titled 'Management Principles (Winter 2026)'

questions.question: How much of my grade comes from my performance as a manager?
questions.referenceAnswer: 5%. The full weighting is in-class activities including case discussion, quizzes, exit tickets and Task 8 feedback at 50%, performance as a manager 5%, skiplevel 1-on-1 5%, Tasks 1-3 combined 5%, Task 4 5%, Task 5 5%, Task 6 5%, Task 7 5%, Task 9 10%, and the Reflection 5%.

questions.question: How many elements does our Overview page need to be eligible for a 4.0?
questions.referenceAnswer: 10 elements. The tiers are 5 elements for a maximum grade of 2.0, 7 for a maximum of 3.0, and 10 for the top standard, a maximum of 4.0. The task also requires visiting the web presence of at least 5 similar or related organizations as market research first.

questions.question: Which channel is required for grade-related discussion?
questions.referenceAnswer: Canvas. The instructor's stated preference order is public Discord message, then private Discord message, then private Canvas message, then email to kaylea@uw.edu only if absolutely necessary, but she notes specifically that all grade-related discussion must happen via Canvas.

questions.question: If Professor Champion has not answered my message in three days, what does the syllabus say to do?
questions.referenceAnswer: Nudge her with a Discord DM. She commits to responding within 48 hours and asks that you nudge her via Discord DM if she has not; the delay is unintentional and is not your fault. A polite and focused request receives a faster reply.

questions.question: What does Task 2 require me to complete individually?
questions.referenceAnswer: At least one LinkedIn Learning tutorial of 45 minutes or more (options include Figma, Canva, Miro, GitHub, or others by approval), and you must share your thoughts on the tool and tutorial via Discord. You turn in a screenshot of your LinkedIn Learning completion certificate, and the instructor also examines your Discord post. The group-level part is contributing to the tool discussion, with the final decision reached by consensus and relayed by the manager.
questions.sourceSection: Project Task 2 Specification: Communication and Prototyping Tools

questions.question: What is the Task 6 SWOT analysis supposed to be about?
questions.referenceAnswer: AI. Task 6 asks you to perform a SWOT analysis with respect to AI: the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats for your organization, product and organizational unit. You deliver a four-quadrant summary grid of bullet points plus a details document explaining each bullet, turned in as a link.
questions.sourceSection: Project Task 6 Specification: Responding to Disruptive Technologies

questions.question: Is a 1,700 word reflection essay acceptable?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The Reflection must be 1000-1500 words. The syllabus says under 900 words is very unlikely to achieve the depth she is seeking, and over 1600 words is unfair to others, so 1,700 is over the stated limit.
questions.sourceSection: Final Paper: Reflection on Management Principles

questions.question: In Task 5, what do we have to work out besides how many people we need?
questions.referenceAnswer: Working conditions (how and where work is done, and what that costs), other costs such as manufacturing, equipment, licensing, training and raw materials, and sources of revenue including projections about what revenue you will make and when the unit might turn a profit. Pay is decided alongside headcount as part of identifying human resources. The deliverable is a narrative or detailed presentation document including proposed structure, budget and projections with contributions visible.

questions.question: How do I actually request my one 48-hour extension?
questions.referenceAnswer: Through Canvas, so that the request is private and trackable. The extension is no questions asked and may be used on one task among Tasks 1-6, once per quarter. The instructor suggests not using it unless you cannot avoid it, since assignments build on one another and you might need it later.

questions.question: During a week when I am acting as manager, what should I arrange if I cannot attend?
questions.referenceAnswer: Arrange to swap duties with a team member. Beyond filing the class absence form, the syllabus adds specifically that if you must miss class, be late, or leave early on a week you are assigned to be the manager, you should arrange to swap duties with a teammate.

questions.question: Is there a way to earn extra credit?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes, one. If your group meets up outside class for non-work purposes, take a selfie and send it to the instructor for a little extra credit. It is available only once, only during the first 3 weeks of the quarter, and only one group member needs to send it.

questions.question: A reading is still marked [To Be Decided] four days before it is due. Do I have to do it?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The instructor commits to never changing readings less than six days before they are due, so a reading marked '[To Be Decided]' that has not been filled in six days before it is due is dropped. The opposite rule applies to '[Tentative]' items: if they are not changed before the deadline, they are assigned.

questions.question: Do I need to buy a textbook?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. There is no required textbook. You engage with material from a wide range of sources, all of which should be free of charge provided you use the version on Canvas or the UW Library Proxy. If you have difficulty accessing any material, tell the instructor right away via a public message on Discord.

questions.question: Does this course require any programming experience?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. Although the catalog description mentions a software project, the instructor points out that the course has only writing prerequisites, not technical ones, and therefore cannot require you to write code. The work focuses on the early stages of a software project - plans, requirements and designs. You express your design in technical form, but there is no requirement to write code or produce software. The prerequisite is CSS 301, which may be taken concurrently.

questions.question: Do I have to attend the open coworking periods?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The syllabus states that attending open coworking periods and office hours is optional. Open coworking periods are drop-in times to ask questions and work on assignments with help at hand; she announces them in the weekly announcement email and on Discord.
questions.sourceSection: The synchronous elements of the course

questions.question: Do sources produced by an AI tool need to be credited in my work?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes. All sources, including AI tools, must be properly cited. AI-based tools are permitted on some assignments, with each assignment's instructions specifying whether and how, and use inconsistent with those parameters is treated as academic misconduct subject to investigation. Using information without proper citation, including from AI tools, counts as plagiarism, and fabricated citations are themselves a form of academic dishonesty.
questions.sourceSection: Use of AI Tools / Academic Dishonesty

questions.question: What is the deadline for the prototyping and communication tools task?
questions.referenceAnswer: Friday, January 30th. That is Project Task 2, on communication and prototyping tools. As with most assignments in the course, work is due at 11:59 p.m. Pacific time on the listed day.
questions.sourceSection: Project Task 2 Specification: Communication and Prototyping Tools

questions.question: How many students will be on my project team?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not specify a team size. It says groups are assigned and announced in class, that the instructor collects confidential feedback on how groups are functioning, and that she reserves the right to rearrange group membership to support everyone's learning, but no number of students per group appears anywhere.

questions.question: Do we need a paid Jira account for the group project?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not say. It requires the team to create a Jira board in Task 1, requires the manager to update it and submit screenshots, and lists Jira among the behavioral traces used for assessment, but it says nothing about which Jira plan or tier to use, whether a paid account is needed, or who would pay for it.
questions.sourceSection: Project Task 1 / Weekly Team Meetings (not specified)

questions.question: What happens to my grade if my group never assigns me a manager rotation?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not address this. It states that management rotates among group members, that you act as manager during a two-week span, and that performance as a manager is 5% of the grade, and the schedule even notes that not all groups have a manager in a given week. But no rule is given for what happens to that 5% if a student never takes a rotation. The correct behavior is to say the syllabus does not specify and suggest raising it with the instructor, not to invent a reweighting.
questions.sourceSection: Grading / Doing the project as a manager (not specified)

questions.question: How far ahead do I need to book office hours, and what should I do if I have to cancel?
questions.referenceAnswer: Book at least 24 hours in advance, because a booking made less than 24 hours ahead may be missed; if you do book late, ping her on Discord to confirm. To cancel, use the 'cancel' link included in the booking rather than just declining the meeting.
questions.sourceSection: Contact / The synchronous elements of the course

questions.question: When and where does CSS 350 meet?
questions.referenceAnswer: Tuesday and Thursday, 5:45 PM to 7:45 PM, in UW1 building room 220.

questions.question: What do we actually have to have finished to be done with Task 1?
questions.referenceAnswer: You are done with Task 1 when you have a team name, an essential scope/concept, and an organization type. You turn in a link to the team Google doc containing your name and scope/concept, plus a screenshot of your Jira board. All group members and Dr. Champion need invites to and should join all group environments. It is due Friday, January 23.

questions.question: How many elements does our Overview or About Us page need if we are going for a 4.0?
questions.referenceAnswer: 10 elements. The tiers are 5 elements for a maximum grade of 2.0, 7 elements for a maximum of 3.0, and 10 elements for the top standard, a maximum of 4.0. The task also requires visiting the web presence of at least 5 similar or related organizations as market research first.

questions.question: What is the Task 6 SWOT analysis supposed to be about?
questions.referenceAnswer: AI. Task 6 asks you to perform a SWOT analysis with respect to AI: the strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats for your organization, product, and organizational unit. You deliver a four-quadrant summary grid of bullet points plus a details document explaining each bullet, turned in as a link. It is due Friday, February 27 at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time.
questions.sourceSection: Project Task 6 Specification: Responding to Disruptive Technologies

questions.question: When is the final version of the company project due?
questions.referenceAnswer: Thursday, March 19. That is Task 9, the final version of your organization and prototype. Note that although the packet is assembled with your group, Task 9 is an individual submission, and you submit all links and media needed to assess the project and your contribution.

questions.question: How much of my grade depends on how I do as a manager?
questions.referenceAnswer: 5%. The full weighting is in-class activities including case discussion, quizzes, exit tickets, and Task 8 feedback at 50%, performance as a manager 5%, skiplevel 1-on-1 5%, Tasks 1-3 combined 5%, Task 4 5%, Task 5 5%, Task 6 5%, Task 7 5%, Task 9 10%, and the Reflection 5%.

questions.question: What percentage do I need for a 2.0 in this class?
questions.referenceAnswer: 74.6%. The instructor maps an overall 97.0% to a 4.0 and 60.0% to a 0.7 with even spacing in between, which puts a 2.0 at 74.6%.

questions.question: Can I use my 48-hour extension on Task 9?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The one no-questions-asked 48-hour extension per quarter may be used on one task among Tasks 1 through 6 only, requested through Canvas. The syllabus states explicitly that no extension is possible for Task 9 or the Reflection because they sit at the very end of the quarter and grades must be submitted on time, and none is possible for the Demo and Feedback assignments either.

questions.question: It is my week as manager and I have to miss Thursday. What am I supposed to do?
questions.referenceAnswer: Arrange to swap duties with a team member. On top of filing the class absence form, the syllabus adds specifically that if you must miss class, be late, or leave early during a week you are assigned to be the manager, you should arrange to swap duties with a teammate.

questions.question: Do my Discord messages actually count toward my grade?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes. The instructor assesses work based on the evidence she sees in behavioral traces, the records left behind in the tools used for the course. The weekly Management Team Meeting turn-in is explicitly assessed from Discord against the rubric on Canvas, and individual contributors send their team meeting notes to the team chat.
questions.sourceSection: Notes on Group Work / Management Team Meetings

questions.question: Can I use AI to help me write the final reflection essay?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The Reflection on Management Principles explicitly forbids AI tools; it is meant to be an essay only you could write because it is about specific events in your experience of the course. The syllabus also warns that AI tools are notorious for fabricating citations and that fabricated citations are a form of academic dishonesty. The same prohibition applies to the Task 0 and Task 00 manager reflections and to Task 8 feedback.
questions.sourceSection: Final Paper: Reflection on Management Principles

questions.question: Does running my writing through a spellchecker count as prohibited AI use?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The instructor states that she does not consider grammar or spellchecking to be a prohibited use of AI, even on assignments where other AI uses are not allowed.

questions.question: Is there any extra credit in CSS 350?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes, one. If your group meets up outside of class for non-work purposes, take a selfie and send it to the instructor for a little extra credit. It is available only once, only during the first 3 weeks of the quarter, and only one group member needs to send it.

questions.question: What happens in the skiplevel 1-on-1, and how long does it take?
questions.referenceAnswer: It is one 15 minute meeting per person over the whole quarter, scheduled during the last 30 minutes of a class while others do group work; if you do not schedule it during class you have to schedule it during office hours. It is friendly but evaluative, framed as an oral exam: she asks a conceptual course content question with a range of right answers, not trivia or a trick question, and then asks how things are going and what questions you have for her. Nothing is turned in and you receive feedback from her. Her availability is very tight at the end of the quarter, so do not wait.

questions.question: Do I need to know how to program to take this course?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. Although the catalog description mentions a software project, the instructor points out that the course has only writing prerequisites, not technical ones, and therefore cannot require you to write code. The work focuses on the early stages of a software project: plans, requirements, and designs. You express your design in technical form, but there is no requirement to write code or produce software. The prerequisite is CSS 301, which may be taken concurrently.

questions.question: How many people will be on my project team?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not specify a team size. It says groups are assigned and announced in class, that the instructor collects confidential feedback on how groups are functioning, and that she reserves the right to rearrange group membership to support everyone's learning, but no number of students per group appears anywhere.
questions.sourceSection: Notes on Group Work / Schedule (not specified)

questions.question: Can I join class over Zoom on days I am sick?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not establish a remote attendance option, and the correct behavior is to say so rather than invent one. What it does say is that if you must miss class, be late, or leave early you should file the course absence form at least an hour before class, that advance notice lets you avoid a no-call, no-show penalty but does not serve as a makeup, that there is no direct way to make up missed in-class activities, and that you are responsible for obtaining class notes, handouts, and assignments in the event of an absence.
questions.sourceSection: Impact of Missing Class / Your Presence in Class (not specified)

questions.question: Do we need a paid Jira account for the group project?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not say. It requires the team to create a Jira board in Task 1, requires the manager to keep it updated and submit screenshots of it, and lists Jira among the behavioral traces used for assessment, but it says nothing about which Jira plan or tier to use, whether a paid account is needed, or who pays for it.
questions.sourceSection: Project Task 1 / Weekly Team Meetings (not specified)

questions.question: How much of my final grade comes from the third sprint?
questions.referenceAnswer: Sprint 3 is 15% of the final grade. The full weighting is in-class activities including case discussion 50%, Sprint 1 10%, Sprint 2 15%, Sprint 3 15%, Presentation (pre-made demo and feedback) 5%, and Reflection 5%.

questions.question: What overall percentage do I need to end up with a 4.0 in this course?
questions.referenceAnswer: 97.0%. The instructor maps an overall 97.0% to a 4.0 and 60.0% to a 0.7, with even spacing in between, which means a 2.0 requires 74.6%.

questions.question: I think one of my scores was entered wrong. How long do I have to bring it up?
questions.referenceAnswer: Within 1 week of the grade being released, by booking a private timeslot on the instructor's calendar. In that consultation you are expected to take the lead and show in specific detail how your work fulfills the rubric for the assignment type, how you met the criteria for that specific assignment, and how it meets the course learning goals.

questions.question: Professor Champion has not replied to my message in three days. What does the syllabus tell me to do?
questions.referenceAnswer: Nudge her with a Discord DM. She commits to responding within 48 hours and asks that you nudge her via Discord DM if she has not; a missed message is unintentional and is not your fault. A polite and focused request gets a faster reply.

questions.question: How long is the Reflection essay supposed to be?
questions.referenceAnswer: 800 to 1200 words. Under 800 is unlikely to achieve the depth the instructor is looking for, and over 1200 is described as unfair to others. It must be a standard essay with an introduction, key points, and a conclusion, in a consistent formatting standard such as APA, Chicago, or ACM.
questions.sourceSection: Reflection on Software Engineering and the Bot Project

questions.question: How long should our pre-made demo video be, and does the whole group share one recording?
questions.referenceAnswer: 2 to 5 minutes, and no, the group does not share one. Each group member records their own screen capture video of the bot in action with a voiceover and uploads their own video to Canvas, one per student. It is due Monday, November 24 at 11:59 p.m.

questions.question: For the live demo, do we plug our laptop into the projector?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. To avoid awkwardness around switching laptops, the podium computer drives the projector and all presenting laptops join a Zoom room and screenshare to present. Live demos are in class on Tuesday, November 25, in a 10 minute slot, with time for questions afterward.

questions.question: What are we supposed to do if the bot breaks in the middle of our live demo?
questions.referenceAnswer: Fall back on the pre-made demos. In case of live demo failure the syllabus says to be prepared to share 2 of your pre-made demos so that you can still get good feedback.

questions.question: Which Bot Project task covers releasing version 2.0, and what date is it set for?
questions.referenceAnswer: Bot Project Task #6, due November 21, a Friday, at 11:59 p.m. Seattle time. It requires each member to complete at least one user story from the second sprint, deploy version 2.0 to the production environment, and tag the code so it is clear which version is 2.0.
questions.note: Reworded from a plain 'When is version 2.0 due?' phrasing, which tripped the surface-form check against the trained 'When is the Bot Feedback due?'. The underlying fact (Task #6 / v2.0 / November 21) appears in no training or validation example.

questions.question: Besides the written report, what does Task 5 want from us?
questions.referenceAnswer: User stories. Task 5 is done when the group has published a single shared code analysis report to the main group repository and created user stories drawn from both the problems found and any new ideas for improving the bot. There is no artifact turn-in; the state of your repository and project board is graded directly.

questions.question: Do I need to buy a textbook for this course?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. There is no required textbook. You engage with material from a wide range of sources, all of which should be free of charge as long as you use the version on Canvas or the UW Library Proxy. If you have trouble accessing any material, tell the instructor right away with a public message on Discord.

questions.question: Could I actually be dropped from CSS 360 for missing the first week?
questions.referenceAnswer: Yes, if the class is full. Many students request to join and there are not always enough seats, so the instructor may need to drop anyone who misses the first two class sessions and replace them with unenrolled students who do attend. She notes this is consistent with college policy and with the course description in the catalog.

questions.question: Can I paste my bot's Discord API token into ChatGPT to help me debug an auth error?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The syllabus says to be very careful with API tokens and secrets: do not exchange them via public channels, do not commit them into GitHub, and do not paste them into AI tools or search engines. AI tools are welcome as a tutor and debugging aid generally, but not with secrets in the prompt.
questions.note: Deliberately probes whether a model over-generalizes the trained 'AI tools are fine for debugging' answer to a case the syllabus carves out.

questions.question: When our sprint is finished, should we open a pull request back to the class's original repository?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. You should consider your fork a hard fork. The instructor does not expect, and says she does not want, a pull request merging your group's code into the class's default code; you take the basic shell and head in your own direction. Pull requests are for merging into your own team's main branch.

questions.question: A reading is still marked [To Be Decided] and class is in four days. Do I still have to do it?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The instructor commits to never changing readings less than six days before they are due, so a reading marked '[To Be Decided]' that has not been filled in six days before it is due is dropped. The opposite rule applies to '[Tentative]' items: if they are not changed before the deadline, they are assigned.

questions.question: Can I use my one 48-hour extension on the Bot Feedback assignment?
questions.referenceAnswer: No. The single no-questions-asked 48-hour extension applies only among Bot Project Tasks 1 through 7. No extension is possible for the Demo and Feedback assignments because they involve coordinating the entire class community on very tight timing, and no extension is possible for the Reflection because it sits at the very end of the quarter.
questions.note: Training covers the eligible side of this policy (extensions on Tasks 1-7). This asks about the excluded side, which is a separate sentence.

questions.question: Can I turn Task 5 in four days late if I email Professor Champion before the deadline?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not establish this. It provides one no-questions-asked 48-hour extension per quarter, on one task among Bot Project Tasks 1 through 7, requested through Canvas so the request is private and trackable. A four-day extension and an email-based approval route are not covered anywhere, so the correct behavior is to say the syllabus does not answer this and point to the 48-hour Canvas route. The only other provision is the UWB incompletes policy for a severe or extraordinary interruption.

questions.question: How many points is each in-class quiz worth?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not specify this. It says only that any quizzes will be short and low-stakes and that there will be no exams, and that in-class activities including case discussion account for 50% of the grade as a single combined category. No per-quiz point value is given.

questions.question: What test coverage percentage does our bot code have to hit?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not set any test coverage requirement. It tells you to commit often and test often, and Task 5 asks you to analyze bugs, gaps, and technical debt including by running automated tools on your code, but no coverage threshold or percentage appears anywhere.

questions.question: One of my teammates stopped contributing. How much will my individual grade be adjusted to make up for it?
questions.referenceAnswer: The syllabus does not define any grade adjustment for this. It says group process is key, that work is assessed from behavioral traces left in the course tools, that the instructor collects confidential feedback on how groups are functioning, and that she reserves the right to rearrange group membership to support everyone's learning. No compensating grade formula is stated, so the correct behavior is to say so and point to the confidential feedback route.
